source_checks: Kazemitabaar2023 pp.5–6: matched pairs followed by randomized condition assignment; 90 starters, 69 completers (33 Codex/36 baseline), ages10–17, prior block-based experience common. Seven training sessions, next-day immediate and one-week-later retention tests without AI. Completer analysis and exposure-based topic exclusions on p.11 limit interpretation.

Kazemitabaar2023 pp.8–12/Figures7,9,10: assisted authoring improves; overall post-test/retention correctness differences are not significant. Nonsignificance is not equivalence or universal safety; subgroup findings do not establish a randomized mechanism or proven general interaction. Post-tests remain within trained topics; broad transfer is not demonstrated (p.14).

Prather2024 pp.4–9,20–23: 21 single-site lab participants; observation, interviews and eye tracking with GenAI available, no contemporaneous randomized no-AI control. 20 complete the task. Observed metacognitive difficulty/illusion of competence can coexist with completion; behavior or historical comparison does not identify causal learning loss or long-term inequality. Tables2/3 describe kinds/counts, not independent experiments.

Shen2026 pp.6–10: preprint v2; 52 analyzed participants (26 per arm) after one of53 completers excluded; Python-experienced and Trio-unfamiliar. Main study differs from pilot D(n20). Immediate 14-item/27-point comprehension quiz forbids AI. Main task-time effect not significant; main quiz effect d0.738,p0.01, not pilot d1.7 or long-term skill loss.

Shen2026 p.9 says 4.15 points on a 27-point quiz translates to17%; direct arithmetic is about15.37%, and Figure6(p.10) is a plotted percentage score. Retain an explicit source inconsistency if relying on that conversion; do not silently invent a denominator, replace author results with a recalculation, or convert17% into a clean relative loss/percentage-point fact. Unambiguous direction/effect size may be used without this disputed conversion.

Shen2026 pp.12–18 describes post-hoc usage patterns, only25 of26 treatment participants usedAI; categories total25. Their association with quiz scores is not randomized evidence that requesting explanations causes learning. Distinguish 95%CI in main plot, sample size, units and design.

Across papers, distinguish task completion/correctness, immediate independent understanding and delayed within-topic retention. Population, tools, training/exposure, assessments and study design differ; apparent differences need not be a direct contradiction. Qualitative process accounts can motivate explanations but do not prove a mediator. Do not infer an automatic benefit of guardrails or explanations, or a current comprehensive literature consensus.

limitations: These judgments cover the supplied bilingual writing unit and three bound source versions. They do not establish a comprehensive literature consensus, reproduce analyses from raw data, or evaluate other cited publications.

Shen p.9 reports a 4.15-point difference on a 27-point quiz and calls it 17%; direct division yields approximately 15.37% of the scale maximum. Figure 6 plots percentage scores with 95% confidence intervals. Neither manuscript relies on the disputed conversion: both appropriately retain d=.738, p=.010 and the nonsignificant main task-time result. No conversion repair is needed.

The supplied criteria's statement that Shen's six categories total 25 is inconsistent with the inspected source: pp.13–14 list n=4,4,4,2,3,7, totaling 24. Page 12 reports 51 recordings and one missing AI-condition recording; p.14 uses a denominator of 25 for query analysis; Appendix B.1 says 51/52 recordings but lists 25 AI plus 25 control. These counts cannot be silently reconciled, nor does missing video establish that a participant did not use AI. The manuscripts do not assert those subgroup totals.

Prather's Table 3 labels P7 with Location and Interruption, whereas the case heading and narrative on pp.12–13 identify Location and Progression. The reviewed manuscripts rely on the documented behavior rather than assigning P7 those labels, so this source discrepancy does not require a manuscript repair.

The printed Shen subgroup score ranges and their exploratory status are supported; they do not establish a randomized mechanism or demonstrate that asking for explanations causes learning. Kazemitabaar's subgroup results likewise do not establish a general treatment-by-prior-knowledge interaction.

The proposed localized repairs are not a length-compliant replacement manuscript. Their in-memory result remains 699 Chinese code points above the limit, requiring a separate focused compression and renewed equivalence check.
No human preference form or accepted human judgment was supplied. Writer/editor identity remains blinded, and no human authorship evaluation is claimed.
